steps.title: Load both quarters' filings
steps.prose: Every Senate LDA filing from the two exports, as filed. Each filing appears once per issue area it names, so a filing naming several issue areas states the same money that many times.
steps.data_description: Every filing, exactly as the export recorded it.

steps.title: Find the rows that mention AI
steps.prose: A search for six terms in each filing's own words — artificial intelligence, AI, machine learning, large language model, deepfake, algorithmic. A net, not a judgment: it also catches algorithmic trading and airline codes on purpose.
steps.data_description: Every filing whose own words used one of the six terms; the rest carry no figure forward.

steps.title: Judge whether the filing is really about AI
steps.prose: A model reads each filing's own words and decides whether the lobbying was about AI itself, or the term is incidental. Trust this step least: read the words yourself before taking its answer.
steps.data_description: The same filings, plus the model's answer and the sentence it based that answer on.

steps.title: Keep only what the model read as being about AI
steps.prose: A filing the model called incidental is dropped here, and a filing it left no answer for is dropped too — no answer is not a yes.
steps.data_description: The filings the model read as really about AI.

steps.title: Read the reported money
steps.prose: The two money fields as plain dollar numbers. Blank means the filing is reporting it received or spent nothing. Anything else that is not a plain number stops the run rather than being guessed at.
steps.data_description: The same filings, with their reported money read as numbers.

steps.title: Tell paid lobbying from in-house
steps.prose: A filing whose registrant and client are the same name, exactly as filed, is lobbying an organisation did with its own staff. Everything else is one organisation paying another.
steps.data_description: The same filings, each marked paid-to-a-firm, in-house, or a new registration.

steps.title: Collapse each filing back to one entry
steps.prose: A filing that named several issue areas is several rows until here; this puts it back to one. Where its rows disagree on a field, the run stops rather than picking one.
steps.data_description: One entry per filing that survived every prior step.

steps.title: Set the paid filings apart
steps.prose: The filings where a client paid an outside firm — the ones behind the headline figure.
steps.data_description: The paid AI filings, before anyone has confirmed them.

steps.title: Put every paid filing in front of a person
steps.prose: The model's reading is only a proposal: every filing behind the headline figure waits here for a person to confirm or overturn it, under their own name, largest reported spend first.
steps.data_description: The same paid filings, plus the answer a person left on each.

steps.title: Drop what a person did not confirm
steps.prose: A filing the reviewer overturned leaves here; its money enters no published figure.
steps.data_description: The paid AI filings a person confirmed.

steps.title: Publish the headline figures
steps.prose: What clients paid outside firms to lobby on AI: the total, the filings behind it, and the paying clients — plus the same total split by client. Open it under Published.
steps.data_description: The confirmed paid filings, summed as the published totals.

steps.title: Total what organisations reported for their own AI lobbying
steps.prose: Reported separately and never added to the paid total — an organisation's own account of what it spent lobbying with its own staff, on the model's reading alone. Nobody reviews this branch, and the report says so.
steps.data_description: The in-house AI filings and their reported total, unreviewed.

steps.title: Size the corpus this question was asked of
steps.prose: How many filings the two exports carried in total, before any prior step narrowed them — the base rate the AI figures should be read against.
steps.data_description: How many filings the two exports carried, in total.
